aciklama: Elevation, road surface and winter closures of {n} mountain passes in {c} countries, from the Motoseyir pass database: tables by region and country.
lead: The Motoseyir pass database lists {n} mountain passes in {c} countries. They range from {lo_ad} at {lo_m} m to {hi_ad} at {hi_m} m, and the median pass lies at {med} m. This page shows the numbers behind the pass pages on this site and ends with a line you can copy when you cite them.

kisa.kapali: Passes with known usual closing months

bolge_p: The regions follow the grouping of the app’s own pass list. A pass on a border counts once in the region of its list entry.
ulke_p: {c} countries, ordered by number of passes. A pass on a border is counted in each of its countries, so the rows add up to more than {n}.
kis_p: For {kapali} passes the database holds the months in which the road is usually closed to motor vehicles. The most common periods:
kis_not: A pass without closing months is not necessarily open all year; it only means the database has no such entry. Opening and closing dates change with the snow every year, so check the road authority before you ride.
sayfa_h2: The ten highest with their own page
sayfa_p: These passes have a page on this site with location, surface, closing months and nearby passes.
metot: The pass list is the one inside the Motoseyir app. It combines a hand-kept list with compilations from OpenStreetMap, which map named passes on roads that can be ridden; most entries point to a Wikipedia or Wikidata page. Elevation is the value in that data, in metres.

Surface (unpaved) and usual closing months appear only where the data has them. US entries were checked against Wikipedia coordinates, and on 28 October 2026 three entries whose tags had been copied from another pass were removed.
The counts show how many passes are in this database, not how many passes a country has. They depend on what is mapped and tagged, so a country with a low count may simply be less covered.

cite_atif: Contains data from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) and Wikidata.

About Motoseyir and how the data is made

sss.s: How many mountain passes does Motoseyir list?
sss.c: {n} passes in {c} countries, in the data snapshot of {tarih}. {n_abd} of them are in the United States, {n_alp} in the Alps and {n_tr} in Türkiye.

sss.s: Which is the highest pass in the Motoseyir database?
sss.c: {hi_ad} in {hi_ulke} at {hi_m} m. The lowest entry is {lo_ad} in {lo_ulke} at {lo_m} m, and the median is {med} m.

sss.s: Does the list show every pass in a country?
sss.c: No. It reflects what the app’s pass data and its OpenStreetMap sources contain, so a country’s count tells you about data coverage, not about how many passes exist there.
